question:
In an electromagnetic wave, energy is transported through space even though there are no charge carriers in free space. A student makes the following claim:

"Since there are no moving charges in free space, an electromagnetic wave cannot carry energy. The fields only ‘exist’ but do not do any real work."

Evaluate this claim using the idea of energy flow in electromagnetic waves (Poynting vector concept) and the fact that EM waves can transfer energy to matter.

Which option best evaluates the statement?

options.A: Incorrect. EM waves carry energy and momentum; energy flow is along $\vec S=\dfrac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec E\times\vec B)$ even in free space.
options.B: Correct. Without charges, $\vec E$ and $\vec B$ cannot store energy, so energy transfer is impossible.
options.C: Correct. EM waves carry only momentum, not energy, because average power in free space is zero.
options.D: Incorrect only for very high frequencies (like X-rays); low-frequency waves (radio) cannot carry energy.
